message: Could Rohin’s reported C2 example—comparing competing predictions with one calculation, then carrying the correction into the next choice—help you judge an actual change in Whiskers’s scene? In your feather passage, what distinguishes the touch against her skin from the sound she hears? Would thinking longer settle that distinction, or would drafting one revised sentence provide better evidence? What thinking or writing step will you choose and complete now? What observation in the wording would make you reconsider that choice? What finding from this draft, remaining uncertainty, and unfinished next step will you carry into your next turn?
